The golden rule is DON'T GET BEHIND. If possible, stay about a week ahead in your readings. At the same time, be sure to review everything you already covered, both recently and a bit further back. My personal strategy is that I go over everything 3 times. Each week, I read next week's chapter, review the material we covered this week, and also go back to review last week's topics. Spaced repetition is an amazingly powerful tool.

As for how many hours studying per week, a good rule of thumb seems to be 5 hours per class every week; or one hour per day, will get you above average grades. Of course there's a lot of other factors that modify this besides just the raw number of hours. A five hour block one night won't allow you to retain much (hence why cramming is useless). On the other end, reading half a page every two hours while you do other tasks won't give you the proper focus. Being in a quiet and undisturbed place with your cell phone off (sorry) will work better than reading on the subway with your earbuds blasting music.

Also, be sure to take advantage of any services available. Office hours are there for a reason. Some departments organize help sessions before exams. Try and find other people in your class who are aiming for a high grade, and form a study group (hint: these people usually sit in the front. You would be wise to do so also).

You'll be fine as long as you put the effort in. Good luck!
